revisionCards.title: Amount of garbage produced by Delhi per day in metric tonnes
revisionCards.explanation: Amount of garbage produced by Delhi per day in metric tonnes.

slides.headline: 📋 Case Question
slides.body: Amount of garbage produced by Delhi per day in metric tonnes.

slides.headline: 🧩 Core Framework
slides.body:
**Framework**: Macro Waste Stream Sourcing (Households + Factories + Hospitals + Commercial Businesses)

**Key Assumptions**:
• Delhi population baseline standard: 3 Crores (~75 Lakh families assuming an average size of 4).
• Delhi spatial area: 1,500 square kilometers, with 3% (~45 sq km) hosting industrial zones.
• Socioeconomic household division: High Income 20%, Middle Income 40%, Low Income 40%.
• Interviewer Constraint: Calculate the final cumulative output metrics in Metric Tonnes per day.

slides.headline: 🪜 Step-by-Step Approach
slides.body:
1. Calculate Household Waste: High-income (>25L) families generate 10kg bio + 10kg non-bio waste daily. Middle-income (5-25L) generate 7.5kg bio + 5kg non-bio. Low-income (<5L) generate 10kg bio + 2kg non-bio. Total Residential = 10.35 Crore kg/day.
2. Calculate Industrial Waste: Out of 11,000 active factories in industrial areas, half are small scale (500 kg/day waste output) and half are large scale (2,500 kg/day waste output). Total Industrial = 3.3 Crore kg/day.
3. Calculate Clinical Medical Waste: Mapped at 6,000 neighborhood clinics (producing 20 kg/day each) and 100 multispecialty hospitals (producing 700 kg/day each). Total Clinical = 2 Lakh kg/day.
4. Calculate Commercial Business Waste: 1 Lakh retail shops produce 10 kg/day each (= 10L kg). 300 shopping malls produce 300 kg/day each (= 90,000 kg). 5 Lakh styling salons produce 10 kg/day each (= 50L kg). Total Commercial = ~61 Lakh kg/day.
5. Sum the global system streams (`10.35 Cr kg + 3.3 Cr kg + 0.02 Cr kg + 0.61 Cr kg = 14.28 Crore kg/day`).
6. Convert total weight metric to Metric Tonnes (divide kg value by 1,000 constant).

slides.headline: 🧮 Mathematical Model
slides.body:
**Formula**:
`Daily Waste = [Households (10.35 Cr) + Factories (3.3 Cr) + Hospitals (0.02 Cr) + Businesses (0.61 Cr)] / 1000`

slides.headline: 🏆 Final Estimate
slides.body:
Estimated final result:

**~140,000 Metric Tonnes of waste generated per day**

revisionCards.title: Number of liters of water consumed in India per person
revisionCards.explanation: Estimate number of liters of water consumed in India per person (For personal use only).

slides.headline: 📋 Case Question
slides.body: Estimate number of liters of water consumed in India per person (For personal use only).

slides.headline: 🧩 Core Framework
slides.body:
**Framework**: Activity Bottom-Up Aggregation (Drinking + Bathing + Washing + Cleaning + Cooking)

**Key Assumptions**:
• Water calculation accounts explicitly for personal daily activities; macro industrial/agricultural layers are filtered out.
• Household baseline matches a standard Indian family unit of 5 members.
• Economic and access variables can skew individual use parameters up or down by a 10L baseline range.

slides.headline: 🪜 Step-by-Step Approach
slides.body:
1. Drinking: 7.5 glasses of 200ml fluid = 1.5 Liters/day per capita.
2. Bathing & Hygiene: Mapped at 1 standard storage bucket + 5L for sanitary chores = 45 Liters/day.
3. Washing Clothes: Family of 5 consuming 15 buckets (40L each) once every 3 days. Per capita daily allocation = 40 Liters/day.
4. Washing Utensils: Consuming 2.5 buckets (40L each) daily for the family unit. Per capita daily allocation = 20 Liters/day.
5. Vehicle Cleaning: 2 buckets per day to clean family cars/scooters. Shared household allocation = 16 Liters/day.
6. House Cleaning: 1 bucket of water used daily for structural dusting and mopping loops. Shared allocation = 8 Liters/day.
7. Minor Hygiene & Culinary Cooking: Handwashing (12 cycles at 200ml each = 2.4L) + cooking preparation steps (1.5L per meal across 3 shared cycles = 0.9L per capita). Total minor = 3.3 Liters/day.
8. Sum the individual volume metrics (`1.5 + 45 + 40 + 20 + 16 + 8 + 3.3 = 133.8 Liters`).

slides.headline: 🧮 Mathematical Model
slides.body:
**Formula**:
`Per Capita Consumption = Drinking + Bathing + Laundry + Utensils + Asset Cleaning + Cooking`

slides.headline: 🏆 Final Estimate
slides.body:
Estimated final result:

**On average 130 to 140 Liters of water consumed per person per day**

revisionCards.title: Average distance traveled by cycle by an Indian
revisionCards.explanation: Estimate the average distance travelled by cycle by an Indian.

slides.headline: 📋 Case Question
slides.body: Estimate the average distance travelled by cycle by an Indian.

slides.headline: 🧩 Core Framework
slides.body:
**Framework**: Active Inventory Pool ÷ Gender-Regional Active Commuters

**Key Assumptions**:
• Annual national bicycle unit sales constant: 1.61 Crore cycles.
• Average operational lifespan of a bicycle in the country: 5 Years (Total active national inventory = 8.05 Crore units).
• Interviewer Constraint: Compute the net mathematical average distance covered across exactly 1 day.

slides.headline: 🪜 Step-by-Step Approach
slides.body:
1. Establish the nationwide active bicycle stock base (`1.61 Cr × 5 years = 8.05 Crore` operating cycles).
2. Divide active ownership into gender-regional active commuter nodes scaled on a per-day track (divide by 365):
3.   - Urban Females: 12.33 Lakh active riders logging 7.5 km daily for work transits, core exercises, or errands.
4.   - Urban Males: 56.6 Lakh active riders logging split distances based on age (0-18: 5 km/day; 18-50: 7.5 km/day; 50+: 0 km).
5.   - Rural Females: Household constraints mean platform activity profiles scale near zero (~0).
6.   - Rural Males: 61.64 Lakh active riders utilizing cycles as primary transit, logging a high 10 km daily to work zones.
7. Run a weighted average matching total tracked distance against the active commuter pools.

slides.headline: 🧮 Mathematical Model
slides.body:
**Formula**:
`Average Distance = Sum of (Demographic Rider Volumes * Daily Travel Metrics) / Total Active National Cycles`

slides.headline: 🏆 Final Estimate
slides.body:
Estimated final result:

**6.8 km is estimated to be the average distance travelled by cycle in India daily**

revisionCards.title: Average distance run by a football player in an average match
revisionCards.explanation: Estimate the average distance run by a football player in an average match.

slides.headline: 📋 Case Question
slides.body: Estimate the average distance run by a football player in an average match.

slides.headline: 🧩 Core Framework
slides.body:
**Framework**: Tactical Position Partitioning (Goalkeeper vs. Defender vs. Midfielder vs. Attacker) x Velocity Phase Run-Rates

**Key Assumptions**:
• Standard game timeline: 90 Minutes (ignore extra time/overtime metrics).
• Tactical layout: 4-3-3 formation template on a standard 100m pitch layout (ignore tactical substitutions).
• Possession distribution: Equal 50/50 balance of ball possession between both competing teams.

slides.headline: 🪜 Step-by-Step Approach
slides.body:
1. Goalkeeper: Restricted to penalty area bounds (~15m grid). Tracked across roughly 20 defensive or build-up plays per match (`15m × 20 = 300m`). Net position run = 0.3 km.
2. Establish temporal ball possession weights per tactical line across the 90 minutes: Defenders manage build-ups for 30 mins (3.75 mins/player); Midfielders build attacks for 40 mins (6.67 mins/player); Attackers finish for 20 mins (3.33 mins/player).
3. Map out position-based movement speed arrays (km/hr) across three operational game phases:
4.   - Phase A: Player's team has possession of the ball (Defenders run at 5 km/hr, Midfielders at 8 km/hr, Attackers at 15 km/hr).
5.   - Phase B: Team has possession but player does not have the ball (Defenders at 3 km/hr, Midfielders at 10 km/hr, Attackers at 10 km/hr).
6.   - Phase C: Opposing team holds ball possession (Defenders defend at 10 km/hr, Midfielders at 5 km/hr, Attackers walk at 3 km/hr).
7. Calculate the cumulative distance run for each position tier by multiplying phase run-rates by time spent in each phase:
8.   - Defenders = 9.88 km; Midfielders = 11.03 km; Attackers = 10.03 km.
9. Compute the final weighted mean across the 11 active on-field player nodes (`1 Goalkeeper + 4 Defenders + 3 Midfielders + 3 Attackers`).

slides.headline: 🧮 Mathematical Model
slides.body:
**Formula**:
`Average Match Distance = [(1 * 0.3) + (4 * 9.88) + (3 * 11.03) + (3 * 10.03)] / 11 Players`

slides.headline: 🏆 Final Estimate
slides.body:
Estimated final result:

**9.36 km covered by a football player in an average match**

revisionCards.title: Average electricity consumption in India in a household in a day
revisionCards.explanation: Estimate average electricity consumption in India in a household in a day.

slides.headline: 📋 Case Question
slides.body: Estimate average electricity consumption in India in a household in a day.

slides.headline: 🧩 Core Framework
slides.body:
**Framework**: Lifestyle Archetype Matrix (Urban Luxury vs. Rural Baseline) x Appliance Power Loads (Watts) x Seasonal Run-Rates

**Key Assumptions**:
• Total residential household context baseline: 37.5 Crore families.
• Lifestyle distribution: Urban High-Utility/Digital (40% share); Rural Core/Minimalist (60% share).
• The calendar year is evaluated across an even seasonal split (4 summer months, 4 rainy months, 4 winter months).

slides.headline: 🪜 Step-by-Step Approach
slides.body:
1. Set appliance power ratings (Watts/hr): Ceiling fans 40W, Air Conditioners 1000W, Water Heaters 1500W, Televisions 150W, Lights 30W, Refrigerators 500W, Washing Machines 1000W.
2. Analyze Urban Lifestyle (40% share): High appliance use. Summer profiles include running 3 fans for 16 hours, an AC for 24 hours, a refrigerator for 24 hours, a TV for 4 hours, lights for 8 hours, and smart device charging hooks for 10 hours. Winter profiles swap out the AC for a 2-hour water heater run and a 2-hour washing machine cycle.
3. Analyze Rural Lifestyle (60% share): Stripped-back utility. 30% of households own a basic desert cooler running for 8 hours in the summer. General appliance use scales down to 2 fans running for 16 hours, 6 hours of TV, 8 hours of refrigerator run, and 8 hours of lighting. Winter options drop the cooling units and add brief 1.5-hour water heater loops.
4. Calculate the total operating watt-hours for each lifestyle profile, average them across the seasonal changes, and convert the final value to Kilowatt-hours (kWh or Units) per household.

slides.headline: 🧮 Mathematical Model
slides.body:
**Formula**:
`Average National Daily Consumption = [Urban Year-Round Watt-Hours * 40% + Rural Year-Round Watt-Hours * 60%] / 1000`

slides.headline: 🏆 Final Estimate
slides.body:
Estimated final result:

**Approx. 8 to 12 kWh (Units) consumed per household daily**

revisionCards.title: LPG gas usage in a household per month in India
revisionCards.explanation: Estimate the LPG gas usage in a household per month in India.

slides.headline: 📋 Case Question
slides.body: Estimate the LPG gas usage in a household per month in India.

slides.headline: 🧩 Core Framework
slides.body:
**Framework**: Household Size Constant x Culinary Meal Complexity × Cylinder Volumetric Burn Rates

**Key Assumptions**:
• Total residential household base: 37.5 Crores with a standard family size constant of 4 members.
• A standard household liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinder carries a fixed net fuel weight of 14.2 kg.
• Cooking configurations assume the preparation of 3 hot meals (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) along with intermediate tea/coffee sessions daily.

slides.headline: 🪜 Step-by-Step Approach
slides.body:
1. Establish the standard household model: 4 family members eating cooked meals at home daily.
2. Break down daily cooking times: Factor in boiling water, preparing flour, cooking vegetables, and making tea. This averages roughly 1.5 to 2 hours of active gas burner runtime daily.
3. Map burner gas consumption: A standard domestic stove burner consumes approximately 140 to 180 grams of LPG fuel per hour of active use.
4. Multiply daily fuel consumption by the 30-day monthly calendar cycle to find the total monthly weight depletion.
5. Cross-reference this depletion rate with the standard 14.2 kg cylinder capacity to determine the monthly refill cycle for a typical family.

slides.headline: 🧮 Mathematical Model
slides.body:
**Formula**:
`Monthly LPG Depletion = Daily Burner Runtime (Hours) * Fuel Burn Rate (Grams/Hour) * 30 Days`

slides.headline: 🏆 Final Estimate
slides.body:
Estimated final result:

**Approx. 12 kg to 14.2 kg per month (Equivalent to roughly 1 standard cylinder every 30 to 35 days)**
